title: A champion's reign meets a rising challenger
paragraphs: For seven years, Formula One had belonged almost exclusively to Mercedes. Since the introduction of the hybrid era in 2014, the team had won every Constructors' Championship, while Lewis Hamilton had claimed six of the previous seven Drivers' titles. Entering 2021, another Mercedes championship felt almost inevitable.

Yet there were signs that this season could be different. Red Bull had ended 2020 as the fastest team, and Max Verstappen had established himself as the one driver capable of consistently challenging Hamilton. Honda, preparing to leave Formula One at the end of the season, was determined to bow out on a high, while Red Bull knew this might be their best opportunity yet to end Mercedes' dominance.

Beyond the championship battle, Formula One itself stood on the brink of change. A major overhaul of the technical regulations had been delayed until 2022, meaning teams faced a difficult balance between fighting for one last title under the current rules and preparing for a completely new era. Every development brought to the 2021 car came at the expense of next year's project.

Few expected just how closely matched Mercedes and Red Bull would prove to be. What followed became one of the most intense, controversial and unforgettable championship battles in Formula One history.
